area: game fix: damage jolt now uses Keystone CameraShake instead of hand-rolled sines

find.report_claim: keystone.camera_shake is a deterministic trauma model: seeded sine phases, trauma clamped to 1 and decayed linearly, sample() returning position plus yaw/pitch offsets without mutating any camera, and a JSON shake_report
find.live_evidence: shooter hand-rolled its own jolt inside _sync_scene: amp = min(1, hurt_t / 0.3) * 0.035 applied as sin(time * 55) on x and cos(time * 47) * 0.6 on y, with no rotation offset and no decay model of its own
find.consumer_evidence: nothing in shooter imported keystone.camera_shake, so the module had no game consumer and the game carried a parallel, weaker implementation of the same feature

read: shooter/game.py _sync_scene camera block and the hurt event handler
killed: keeping both models: two shake sources would fight over the same camera each frame
driving the sim from trauma: that would change combat, RNG and the determinism hash
asserting camera return-to-eye against the pre-hit eye: the idle player's eye drifts a fraction of a millimetre, so the check must compare the live eye
analyze.survivor: own one CameraShake, add trauma on the hurt event, sample it while composing onto the sim pose, expose shake_report, and retarget the old test to prove the same intent through the new mechanism

fix.shooter: shooter/game.py imports CameraShake/shake_report, owns one instance (seed 0, amplitude 0.05, rotation 0.012, frequency 18, decay 2.4), adds 0.6 trauma on the hurt event, advances and samples it in _sync_scene while composing position/yaw/pitch onto the sim pose, exposes camera_shake_report while trauma is live, and resets on build_scene; the hand-rolled sine jolt and its now-unused hurt_t local are removed; tests/test_hurt_shake.py retargeted to four tests covering jolt-on-damage, exact composition onto the sim pose, sim hash isolation, and reset on rebuild
